title: Attempt on Distributions of balance indices for critical beta-splitting trees
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact tree identity, source-specific recurrence or explicit limiting obstruction Result: For a split I distributed by q(m,i), the exact quadratic toll is E(m-2I)^2=m^2-2m*(m-1)/H_(m-1), hence asymptotic to m^2 rather than the source m^2/4. Also E min(I,m-I)<=m/H_(m-1), so E|m-2I|=m-O(m/log m), rather than m/2. If S is the external path length and C the Colless index, S-C is the sum of2*min(child sizes). Therefore E(S-C)<=2n*sum_m a(n,m)/H_(m-1)=2n*E continuous leaf depth=O(n log n). Since E S~(3/pi^2)n log^2 n, E C has that same leading constant, twice the source heuristic coefficient. Check: The quadratic identity follows by E[I(m-I)]=m*(m-1)/(2H_(m-1)). The Colless bound uses only the exact clade-count identity and the established mean continuous leaf-depth theorem. It does not rely on the false unrestricted occupation ansatz. Obstruction: The mean Colless correction and one-split quadratic correction do not identify variances, normalized laws or joint distributions of the balance indices. Those remain unsolved here.

title: Attempt on Explicit stationary law of the leftmost Hammersley drift-jump particles
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Explicit stationary law of the leftmost Hammersley drift-jump particles structural calculation Result: The established rank representation can be expanded into a convergent combinatorial density series. Let B=(1=b1<...<bk) be the limiting first-row labels of the insertion tableau, and let q_B be its probability. The first b=bk labels form a uniform permutation, so q_B=(1/b!)*sum over partitions lambda of b with first row length k of f^lambda times the number of standard tableaux of shape lambda with first row B. Independent unit-rate Poisson spacings then give density exp(-xk)*sum_B q_B*product_(i=2..k)[(x_i-x_(i-1))^(b_i-b_(i-1)-1)/(b_i-b_(i-1)-1)!]. Check: Restriction of an insertion tableau to labels at most b is the tableau of the corresponding restricted subword. The last specified first-row entry b pins the first k labels, irrespective of later larger labels. Conditional on B, the Poisson arrival times have independent gamma increments, so every term is a normalized conditional density and nonnegative summation is valid. For k1 this gives Exp(1); known Poissonized LIS formulas give P(X2>x)=exp(-x)*I0(2sqrt(x)) and E X2=e. Obstruction: This repackages a known representation into explicit but rapidly growing finite-tableau coefficients and an infinite sum. It does not establish a new tractable closed joint law or its novelty, and should not be promoted as a full solution to the source request.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0220-explicit-stationary-law-of-the-leftmost-hammersley-drift-jump-particle

title: Attempt on Finite-crossing arcs through a planar Brownian trace
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Reduction to component adjacency and access Result: If both endpoints lie in the same component of the complement of the Brownian trace, an open connected planar set is polygonally connected; removing loops gives a simple arc avoiding the trace entirely. If an arc crosses the trace finitely many times, its complementary intervals give a finite sequence of complement components with touching closures at successive crossing points. Check: A closure contact alone does not ensure an accessible common boundary point. This is why the necessary finite-chain condition was not promoted to an equivalence. Obstruction: Need finite accessible chains for every pair of components, simultaneously for the Brownian trace.

title: Attempt on Sharp intrinsic and extrinsic one-arm exponents in high dimensions
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Reduce the intrinsic limit to a renewal-type statement for the branching-process comparison. Result: The intrinsic one-arm probability is bounded above and below by constants over n (Kozma-Nachmias), and the comparison object is the survival probability of a critical branching process with finite variance, for which n P(survive n generations) -> 2/sigma^2 (Kolmogorov). For the intrinsic arm event the analogous statement would be n P(intrinsic radius >= n) -> a_in where a_in should be 2/V with V the variance of the offspring distribution of the effective branching structure (the cluster explored by intrinsic distance is a branching process with dependent offspring). Existence of the limit therefore reduces to a Kolmogorov-type limit theorem for the intrinsic exploration, which needs the mean-field two-point asymptotics at the level of an exact constant (the lace expansion gives tau_{p_c}(x) ~ A/|x|^{d-2} with an exact constant A, Hara 2008), plus an exact constant for the 'variance' of the exploration, which is the sum of the three-point function's connected part, computable from the lace expansion in principle. The extrinsic limit is harder because the extrinsic arm event mixes intrinsic distance and Euclidean displacement; its bounded-ratio form comes from a second-moment argument that does not give constants. I could not complete either constant. Obstruction: Exact constants for the intrinsic branching structure require second-order lace expansion information.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0066-sharp-intrinsic-and-extrinsic-one-arm-exponents-in-high-dimensions
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

title: Attempt on Divergence of the 1/d expansion of the connective constant
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Combine the known factorial-type lower bound heuristics with Graham's Borel-type bounds. Result: The source cites Graham's Borel-type bounds on the remainder; if the coefficients a_i satisfy |a_i| >= c K^i i! for infinitely many i then the radius is zero, and the computed a_i (Clisby-Liang-Slade) grow consistently with factorial growth. A rigorous proof of divergence would follow from a lower bound on the number of lace diagrams contributing with the same sign at order i, i.e. a non-cancellation statement; the lace expansion for SAW has alternating-sign contributions (pi^{(N)} with sign (-1)^N) so cancellation cannot be excluded without an explicit asymptotic analysis of the diagram sums. A standard trick for proving zero radius is to exhibit a singularity of the generating function at every point of a circle, which is unavailable here since the 'function' is only asymptotic. I tested the computed coefficients' ratio a_{i+1}/a_i (from the source's cited values, not recomputed here): the ratios increase roughly linearly in i, consistent with factorial growth, but 11 terms cannot certify it. No proof; the conjecture is recorded with the concrete criterion (non-cancellation of leading lace diagrams) that would prove it. Obstruction: Alternating-sign lace contributions may cancel; no asymptotic diagram count with sign control.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0097-divergence-of-the-1-d-expansion-of-the-connective-constant
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved
